question: In which year was the first ICC men’s Cricket World Cup played?
solution:
The correct answer is __1975.__

__
 
• The first Cricket World Cup was contested in England as a series of one-day matches of 60 overs per side held in 1975.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Cricket World Cup is an international cricket championship held at four-year intervals. 
 
• It is the premier contest in one-day cricket and one of the most-watched sporting events in the world.
 
• In 1975 the first Cricket World Cup was contested in England as a series of one-day matches of 60 overs per side.
 
• It was held outside England, in India and Pakistan, for the first time in 1987.
 
• The 1987 contest also saw the number of overs per side reduced to 50. 
 
• In 2007 Australia became the first team to win three consecutive World Cup tournaments.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sir Clive Lloyd was the player of the match in the first Cricket World Cup held in England, in 1975.
 
• The next 13th edition of the ICC Cricket World Cup is scheduled for the year 2023 and the World Cup will be hosted by India.
 
• The (ICC) International Cricket Council is the world governing body of cricket, the ICC is headquartered in Dubai, UAE.
